Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 101, verses 1–11:

Makkiyya (Meccan). It contains one hundred and fifty-two letters, thirty-six words, and eleven verses.

Ibn al-Muqri informed me, saying: Ibn Mattar informed us, saying: Ibn Shurayk narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Sulaym narrated to us, saying: Ibn Shubr narrated to us, from Ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites al-Qari'a (The Striking Calamity), Allah, glorified is He, will make his scale heavy with it on the Day of Resurrection." [238] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/426.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity? And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? The Day when mankind will be like scattered moths,﴾ "al-Farash" refers to the birds that fall into the fire. "Al-mabthuth" means scattered, dispersed. Al-Farra' said: "al-Ghawgha'" is locusts, one riding upon another from terror.

﴿And the mountains will be like carded wool.﴾ Like dyed wool that is fluffed and moistened.

﴿As for him whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life﴾ — pleasing, i.e., in Paradise.

﴿But as for him whose scales are light, his mother will be an abyss.﴾ His dwelling and abode is the Fire. Qatada said: "Hawiya" is an Arabic expression; when a man fell into a severe matter he would say: "Hawat ummuh" (may his mother fall). Some said it means "Umm Ra's" (the mother of his head), meaning they will fall into the Fire upon their heads, and Qatada and Abu Salih adopted this interpretation.

﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾ That is, "What is it?" Then He said: ﴿A blazing Fire.﴾

Ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Zayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "Indeed, there is an angel from the angels of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, appointed on the Day of Resurrection over the scale of the son of Adam. He will be brought and made to stand between the two pans of the scale, and his deeds will be weighed. If his scale is heavy, the angels will call out with a voice that all creation hears, by the name of the man: 'Behold, so-and-so has been made happy with a happiness after which there is no misery.' And if his scales are light, the angels will call out: 'Behold, so-and-so has been made wretched with a wretchedness after which there is no happiness.'"

﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity? And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? The Day when mankind will be like scattered moths,﴾ "al-Farash" refers to the birds that fall into the fire. "Al-mabthuth" means scattered, dispersed. Al-Farra' said: "al-Ghawgha'" is locusts, one riding upon another from terror.

﴿And the mountains will be like carded wool.﴾ Like dyed wool that is fluffed and moistened.

﴿As for him whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life﴾ — pleasing, i.e., in Paradise.

﴿But as for him whose scales are light, his mother will be an abyss.﴾ His dwelling and abode is the Fire. Qatada said: "Hawiya" is an Arabic expression; when a man fell into a severe matter he would say: "Hawat ummuh" (may his mother fall). Some said it means "Umm Ra's" (the mother of his head), meaning they will fall into the Fire upon their heads, and Qatada and Abu Salih adopted this interpretation.

﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾ That is, "What is it?" Then He said: ﴿A blazing Fire.﴾

Ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Zayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "Indeed, there is an angel from the angels of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, appointed on the Day of Resurrection over the scale of the son of Adam. He will be brought and made to stand between the two pans of the scale, and his deeds will be weighed. If his scale is heavy, the angels will call out with a voice that all creation hears, by the name of the man: 'Behold, so-and-so has been made happy with a happiness after which there is no misery.' And if his scales are light, the angels will call out: 'Behold, so-and-so has been made wretched with a wretchedness after which there is no happiness.'"
